column5: Technical Education and Skills Development Authority
column6:
The UAQTEA was established through Republic Act No. 10931 providing for free tuition and other school fees in State Universities and Colleges (SUCs), Local Universities and Colleges (LUCs) and state-run Technical Vocational Institutions (STVIs), establishing the Tertiary Education Subsidy and Student Loan Program (SLP), strengthening the Unified Student Financial Assistance System for Tertiary Education (UniFAST), and appropriating funds therefor. 

Free TVET in Post-Secondary State-Run TVIs (STVI) 
         All Filipino learners who shall enroll in any TESDA-registered TVET program leading to a nondegree certificate or diploma (including bundled programs) offered by STVIs shall be eligible for the free TVET provision, provided that they comply with the admission and retention policies and existing residency rules of the STVIs.  
  
Tertiary Education Subsidy (TES)
         The TES program is established to benefit all Filipino learners who shall enroll in postsecondary TVET programs registered under TESDA and offered in all TESDA-recognized privately-run institutions, subject to prioritization and availability of funds, provided that they comply with the admission and retention policies and existing residency rules of the institutions.

column6:
The project title in URS LUDIP 2026-2035 is "URS GAD Livelihood Training and Resource Center", different with the title from CALABARZON RDIP 2023-2028 and here in PIPOL.

Republic Act No. 9710, otherwise known as the Magna Carta of Women was approved on August 14, 2009 which mandates non-discriminatory and pro-gender equality and equity measures to enable women’s participation in the formulation, implementation and evaluation of policies and plan for national, regional and local development. Gender and Development (GAD) – refers to the development perspective and process that is participatory and empowering, equitable, sustainable, free from violence, respectful of human rights, supportive of self-determination and actualization of human potentials. It seeks to achieve gender equality as a fundamental value that should be reflected in development choices and contends that women are active agents of development, not just passive recipients of development. Gender and development approach is not concerned specifically with women, but with the way in which a society assigns roles, responsibilities, and expectations to both men and women. It applies gender analysis to uncover the ways in which men and women work together, presenting results in neutral terms of economics and competence. With the recent economic crisis and poverty increase due to the COVID-19 pandemic, it is important that people are continuously educated of the gender equality as well as be informed of resource and livelihood opportunities attributed to it. As a state higher educational institution responsible to provide and extend a hand to vulnerable people and communities, it is timely and relevant to create a center that is responsive to the needs of times and stakeholders in gender rights and equality, inclusivity and shared facilities and learnings.

column4: Capability Building Program for the expansion of the Assessment and Certification Infrastructure for New and Amended  Training Regulation
column5: Technical Education and Skills Development Authority
column6:
Assessment and Certification is one of the major functions of TESDA. Under the Philippine TVET Competency Assessment and Certification System (PTCACS), TESDA accredits Competency Assessors and Industry
Practitioners/Experts who meet the standard requirements to assess and evaluate the competence of a prospective candidate for National Certification. To fast-track the building and expansion of the Assessment and Certification infrastructure nationwide, the Certification Office (CO) shall continuously conduct the assessment of prospective Regional Lead Assessors (RLAs) in priority and relevant qualifications through Capability Building Program for Prospective Regional Lead Assessors (CBP-RLAs). The conduct of CBP-RLAs is a joint undertaking of the CO, the Qualifications and Standards Office (QSO) and the Industry Experts who developed the Competency Standards (CS) and CATs.

column4: Strengthening the Philippine workforce through Adaptive and Responsive Digital Knowledge (SPARK) Initiative (formerly known as digitaljobsPH)
column5: Department of Information and Communications Technology
column6:
The Philippines, in line with other nations, recognizes the urgent need to
prepare its workforce for the challenges and opportunities brought by the
Fourth Industrial Revolution. The SPARK Initiative—formerly known as
DigitalJobsPH—embodies the Department of Information and Communications
Technology’s (DICT) commitment to creating sustainable, high-quality
employment opportunities. Through targeted upskilling programs, SPARK
empowers Filipinos to become employable in digital and digitally enabled jobs
across ICT-driven sectors.
The initiative equips local talent with competencies required to tap into
emerging digital career pathways while driving growth within regional ICT
ecosystems. The knowledge acquired by SPARK graduates enhances workplace
productivity and supports employers in accelerating digital transformation.
SPARK also stimulates the optimization of Digital Transformation Centers
(DTCs). Training activities encourage greater engagement with local
communities, increase foot traffic, and elevate public awareness of the
government’s efforts to expand ICT capacity. This demonstrates the availability
of dedicated learning spaces and resources for individuals seeking to improve
their digital skills and advance their careers.

DICT’s efforts extend beyond program implementation, as it actively
participates in the Inter-Agency Council for the Development and
Competitiveness of the Philippine Digital Workforce. The Council leads
national initiatives on upskilling, reskilling, and capability-building in digital
technologies, including mapping the country’s digital skills landscape and
developing a roadmap for evolving job roles and technical competencies.
To strengthen ICT competencies and promote employability in the digital
economy, the SPARK Initiative focuses on three core strategies: (1) Developing
training modules aligned with the skills requirements for online employment
and digital entrepreneurship. (2) Delivering technical training sessions to
build practical, industry-relevant capabilities. (3) Promoting digital careers and
technopreneurship, supporting innovation-driven livelihoods and enterprise
development. These combined efforts aim to empower individuals to thrive in
the digital economy and contribute to national competitiveness in the global
market.
The program prioritizes individuals from marginalized and vulnerable sectors
to ensure inclusive development and equitable access to digital opportunities:
1. Women – Addressing barriers to participation caused by social norms,
discrimination, or limited access to resources by empowering women with
digital skills for workforce inclusion.
2. Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) – Providing customized digital training
and assistive support to enable PWDs to access employment, education, and
livelihood opportunities.
3. Persons Deprived of Liberty (PDLs) – Offering education and vocational
training to support rehabilitation and prepare PDLs for reintegration into
society and the workforce.
4. Out-of-School Youth and Adults – Supporting individuals with limited
access to education through skills training that strengthens employability
and livelihood potential.
5. Career Shifters – Providing reskilling programs for individuals transitioning
to digital careers or seeking new employment pathways.
6. Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) – Supporting OFWs through
reintegration programs, skills development, and entrepreneurship
opportunities to ensure sustainable livelihoods upon return.
7. Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) – Providing capacity
building, mentoring, and access to digital tools to enhance competitiveness,
market reach, and sustainability.

column4: Labor Inspection Program (LIP)

The labor inspection program is a mechanism to ensure that establishments employing workers comply with general labor standards, occupational safety and health standards, and other social legislations intended to safeguard the rights of workers to just and humane conditions at work.  
Under Department Order No. 238, Series of 2023, a strategic compliance model and developmental approach has been adopted in the inspection framework, carrying it out in any of the following approaches: (1) Technical and Advisory Visit; (2) Labor Inspection; and (3) Occupational Safety and Health Investigation. 
For micro establishments, the Technical and Advisory Visit (TAV) program aims to build the capacity of community-based micro-establishments toward sustainable compliance with labor standards.  As a convergence program, it also seeks to facilitate easier access to government programs and services instrumental to addressing their compliance gaps: (1) training on Basic Occupational Safety and Health; (2) First-Aid Training; and (3) employee’s compensation.  Likewise, livelihood assistance and productivity trainings will also be provided to further capacitate micro establishments in improving its  business operations.

column4: Enhancement of Security Measure  for Electronic National Certificates (e-NCs)
column5: Technical Education and Skills Development Authority
column6: The Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) has implemented a significant strategy to curb the proliferation of counterfeit National Certificates (NCs) through the institutionalization of E-Certificates. column4: Development of a Generative AI-Powered labor Market Researcher (MVP)
column5: Technical Education and Skills Development Authority
column6:
The Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA), as the primary government agency responsible for technical-vocational education and training (TVET) in the Philippines, plays a crucial role in ensuring that workforce skills align with labor market needs. TESDA is mandated to formulate strategies for skills development, promote industry partnerships, and implement policies that enhance workforce competitiveness. As part of its commitment to addressing labor market mismatches and improving workforce planning, TESDA aims to leverage artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance its skills anticipation mechanisms. This would automate the data collection being currently employed by TESDA through its existing Skills Need Anticipation strategies such as the Workplace and Skills Satisfaction Surveys (WSSS), industry consultations and initiatives through the Area Based and Demand-Driven Strategy which is the central strategy in operationalizing the Agency’s Development Plan.

In 2023, TESDA commissioned the Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS) to provide inputs to the Philippine Labor Market Information System and TESDA’s Skills Anticipation and Prioritization of Skills Requirements (SAPSR) Framework. The enhanced SAPSR framework,  as recommended in the study, addresses skills and labor market challenges by leveraging the broader Labor Market Information System (LMIS), focusing on skills taxonomy, granular data collection, and big data integration to enhance skills mapping and forecasting. It emphasizes institutional collaboration among government agencies, private sectors, and local governments, alongside capacity-building initiatives to improve data collection, analysis, and dissemination.

This proposed project seeks to acquire an AI-driven system that will strengthen labor market intelligence by analyzing large datasets, identifying trends, and generating predictive insights. These insights will support the Agency, policymakers, industry leaders, and training institutions in aligning skills development programs with future workforce requirements, ensuring that training investments are demand-driven and future-proof.

column4: Expansion of the Study on the Employment of TVET Graduates (SETG) and System in Tracing TVET Graduates using T2MIS Data
column5: Technical Education and Skills Development Authority
column6:
The Study on the Employment of TVET Graduates (SETG) is TESDA’s key instrument for evaluating the effectiveness of its TVET programs in preparing graduates for the workforce. This annual tracer study tracks the employment status of TVET graduates and gathers valuable feedback on curriculum, teaching methods, and program design. TESDA has been conducting tracer studies since 2005, evolving from the Impact Evaluation Study of TVET Programs to the Study on the Employability of TVET Graduates (2014-2017), and eventually to the SETG in 2018, which remains the current approach today.

Despite the institutionalization of the SETG, the study still faces several challenges and limitations that hinder its ability to fully capture graduate outcomes. TESDA Training Management Information System (T2MIS), a centralized system for tracking graduates, plays a crucial role in generating the sampling frame for the SETG. However, there are gaps in the data captured by T2MIS which leads to difficulties in tracing graduates and results in a high rate of respondent replacement. 

These challenges, combined with evolving data requirements, underscore the need for continued refinement of the SETG to effectively address data gaps. In view of this, there is a need to expand the current tracer study and establish a system for tracing TVET Graduates using the T2MIS data. 

For the successful implementation of these changes, the expanded SETG will require additional resources, including increased human capacity, enhanced infrastructure, and budgetary support. The enhanced study must cover a broader range of employment indicators, ensuring TESDA’s training programs remain relevant to the labor market and aligned with policy needs, both at the national and local levels.

column4: Overseas Assessment Program
column5: Technical Education and Skills Development Authority
column6:
TESDA as the agency mandated by law to manage and supervise technical education and skills development (TESD) in the country and implement programs geared towards a quality-assured certification system is providing free assessment service to Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) through the Overseas Assessment Program (OAP). The Overseas Assessment Program (OAP) has been one of the forefront services of TESDA where OFWs can validate and certify their competencies acquired through prior training or work experience at their country of employment. OAP started in 2014 has provided services in 2 countries in Asia, and 4 countries in Middle East, and has served a total of 5,976 OFWs. 

In 2020-2021, the conduct of OAP was deferred due to travel restrictions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2022, the Certification Office received requests on conduct of assessment from different countries/sites (Jeddah, Riyadh, Dubai, Singapore) with an estimated 3,412 OFWs waiting for assessment. However, the OAP was deferred yet again due to budgetary constraints. 

For FY 2026, it is projected that over 2,000 Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) will undergo assessment. Given the anticipated rise in travel costs, additional funding is required to ensure the successful implementation of the program. Currently, the program is operating without a dedicated regular budget, with funds being sourced from the scholarship allocation.

column4: YOUTH ENTREPRENEURSHIP PROGRAM (YEP)
column5: Department of Trade and Industry
column6:
The Youth Entrepreneurship Program (YEP) is anchored on Republic Act No. 10679, or the Youth Entrepreneurship Act, which mandates the promotion of youth entrepreneurship as a national strategy for economic development. Launched in 2018 by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) and the MSME Development Council, YEP is a comprehensive initiative designed to empower young Filipinos aged 15-30 by fostering an entrepreneurial mindset and equipping them with essential business skills. Through targeted interventions, the program helps participants unlock their potential to start and sustain business ventures, thereby contributing to national development and economic independence.

YEP is delivered through two core activities annually: "YEP! You Can Be Your Own Boss" and the "YEP Bootcamp for Young Entrepreneurs." These activities focus on instilling entrepreneurial values, connecting youth with mentors and industry leaders, and providing strategic business opportunities. The program offers tailored training sessions, networking platforms, and avenues for financing and market access. Beneficiaries include youth from various sectors, such as indigenous groups, youth with disabilities, and those not in education or employment. By nurturing entrepreneurial talents, YEP aims to build a vibrant ecosystem where young
entrepreneurs thrive, contributing to inclusive and sustainable growth.

The Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) as the authority and forerunner of Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) system in the country continuously aims to upscale the quality of technical-vocational education and training (TVET) programs for the development of a more competitive Filipino workforce.

In its continuous effort to promote quality TVET in the country, the TESDA System for TVET Accreditation and Recognition (STAR) Program has been implemented through the issuance of TESDA Circular No. 68 series of 2022. It is a system that recognizes Technical Vocational Institutions (TVIs) for their accomplishments, innovations and improvements instituted beyond the minimum requirements set in the Unified TVET Program Registration and Accreditation System (UTPRAS) set by TESDA. 

The STAR Program provides basis in classifying programs of TVIS through the STAR Level Award with categories: 1. ONE STAR, 2. TWO STAR, and 3. THREE STAR. The STAR-rated programs of TVIs can serve as model to other institutions that they can benchmark with. The system focuses on the following criteria: 1. Governance and Management, 2. Curriculum and Program Delivery, 3. Support Services, and 4. Program Performance Measures. It utilizes objective and evidence-based criteria, which are translated into numerical points that will correspond to the STAR Level Award of the program.

column4: TESDA SEAL of Integrity for Assessment Centers
column5: Technical Education and Skills Development Authority
column6:
The TESDA SEAL of Integrity is an institution-based award granted to Accredited Assessment Centers which have consistently adhered to TESDA Operating Procedures and quality management principles in the conduct of assessment delegated by TESDA.

The TESDA SEAL of Integrity for Assessment Centers is anchored on the ASEAN Guiding Principles for Quality Assurance and Recognition of Competency Certification Systems and aligned with the requirements of the ISO 17024 Conformity Assessment - General Requirements for Bodies Operating Certification of Persons. The Award shall utilize objective and evidence-based criteria on governance and management; demonstration of principles of accountability; transparency; independence; confidence and standards; continuous improvement and flexibility of services.

column4: Economic Literacy for Media
column5: Philippine Center for Economic Development
column6:
Trainees will learn to make economic news articles and integrate economic concepts in explaining national topics and daily news, including poverty, prices, inflation, loans, household income, allocation and use of land and water resources, and environmental preservation and sustainable development. 

The on-site training will be conducted for two days every year starting in 2027 until 2029. 

The agency will also develop a separate online course with asynchronous sessions. Courses will also be offered once a year. 

The training is open to national and regional media practitioners in journalism, broadcasting, and established digital news providers. 

Scholarships will be provided for selected participants of the onsite and online courses.

column4: Labor Force Survey
column5: Philippine Statistics Authority
column6: The LFS is a nationwide survey of households conducted by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) to gather data on the demographic and socio-economic characteristics of the population. Data from the survey provides information on major labor market trends such as labor force participation and unemployment rates, hours worked, past industries and occupations of currently unemployed persons.

column5: North Eastern Mindanao State University

planning, and business operations. Beneficiaries will participate in hands-on workshops, mentorship
